macro.regime: Pause-then-hike Fed meets a widening two-front Gulf conflict and newly cracking credit
macro.narrative: Entering Monday Oct 12 (US equities trade a normal session; bond/Treasury desks are SIFMA-closed for Columbus Day), the Gulf conflict widened further over the weekend: Houthi forces struck Riyadh's international airport for a second time (Sun Oct 11, after Saturday's attack killed 12 and wounded roughly 300), the Saudi-led coalition called it a 'war crime' and vowed a 'decisive' response, and a tanker was struck by drone near Oman's Sohar anchorage -- yet Brent (~$103) and WTI (~$91.67) held roughly flat rather than spiking further, suggesting the Hormuz/Houthi supply-risk premium is largely priced in. On policy, CME FedWatch (Oct 10) shows traders pricing an 81.6% chance the FOMC holds at the Oct 27-28 meeting but an 83% chance of a December hike -- a 'pause-then-hike' path that defers near-term rate uncertainty into Wednesday's Sept CPI (headline consensus 3.6% y/y vs 3.4% prior; core ~0.2% m/m vs 0.3%), the week's dominant catalyst alongside Fed Chair Warsh's Thursday IMF fireside chat and a parade of Hammack/Waller/Barkin/Collins/Bowman speeches. Credit is a newly cautionary signal: high-yield OAS has widened to ~3.15% (from 2.87% a year ago, 74th percentile of the past decade) with CNBC/State Street calling junk bonds 'flashing yellow' and Morgan Stanley flagging up to 8% annualized private-credit defaults through mid-2027 (software-led), though stress stays concentrated in CCC tier against a still BB-dominated market. China's rare-earth truce (extended 23 Sep by Bessent from its original Nov 10 expiry to Jan 10 2027) remains intact but the White House says shipments still haven't normalized. Bitcoin is stabilizing near $83,600 (+0.69% on the day) and there is no active federal shutdown (the Sept 2 CR funds government through Dec 11), leaving the week's swing factors as CPI, Fed speakers, and whether Saudi retaliation escalates the Gulf conflict further.

Conversely, the truce holding through Jan 10 2027 removes the near-term catalyst that would benefit JL MAG's pricing power, capping upside in that scenario
Faces longer-term competitive erosion as DoD-backed Western alternatives (MP, Lynas, USAR) scale with floor-price offtake support
Less transparent company-level data available versus the US/Australian-listed peers, limiting grounded conviction

calls.name: VanEck Rare Earth and Strategic Metals ETF
drivers: Diversified basket exposure smooths single-name volatility within the rare-earth complex as the Jan 10 2027 truce-expiry date approaches
Benefits broadly from the structural China-export-curb/Western-reshoring narrative described across MP, Lynas and USAR
The truce's unresolved shipment-normalization issue (per the White House) keeps the next quarter a genuine event-risk window for the basket
Western supply-chain readiness is still described as thin, suggesting the re-rating trade has further multi-year room to run regardless of the near-term truce outcome

callsNote: Updated Mon 12 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT; no new session since Friday's close (weekend + pre-Asia-open). The one genuine new input this run is the Gulf conflict's second front -- a Sunday Oct 11 Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport, Saudi Arabia vowing 'decisive' retaliation, and a tanker strike near Oman's Sohar anchorage -- which nudged safe-haven commodities (GLD/SLV/DBC) and defensive factors (USMV) up slightly and broad equity/risk calls (SPY/QQQ/IWM) down slightly versus Sunday's framing, without a full re-rating since Brent/WTI held rather than extended their spike. The second genuinely new input is credit: HY OAS spreads widened to a 74th-percentile ~3.15% ('flashing yellow' per CNBC/State Street) with Morgan Stanley flagging up to 8% annualized private-credit defaults through mid-2027 (software-led) -- this lifted QUAL/XLF conviction (balance-sheet-strength premium) while softening HYG/LQD/IWM (credit-dependent exposure). CME FedWatch's Oct 10 reading (81.6% October hold, 83% December hike) reframes every bond-sleeve call around Wednesday's Sept CPI rather than the FOMC meeting itself. The rare-earth basket (MP/LYC.AX/UUUU/USAR/REMX/6680.HK) is carried forward unchanged from Sunday -- no new truce, filing, or price development surfaced this run.
